end.summary:
Practised the pattern that sums of consecutive odd numbers from 1 are square numbers.
Computed examples through 1+3+5+7+9 = 25 and six odd numbers = 36.
Applied the pattern to odd numbers from 1 to 29: 15 terms, sum 225.
Discussed adding dots around square arrangements; the counting explanation remained incomplete.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised identifying square-number totals by adding consecutive odd numbers and correctly explained several examples, including why 1 through 29 gives 15² = 225. They also explored a dot-arrangement model, using rows, columns, and overlap, but mixed up the number of added dots; this was not corrected by the end. At home, ask them to draw the first six square arrangements and label the new odd-number layer added each time.
